entities.summary:
Leochares was an ancient Greek sculptor from Athens who lived in the 4th century BC. He is known for creating the famous statue of Zeus at Olympia, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Leochares' innovative techniques and use of marble helped establish Athens as a major artistic center during this period.

    The construction of the statue of Zeus was commissioned by Epheus, an Athenian diplomat, who wanted to rival the Egyptian temples in grandeur and artistry. The project took over 12 years to complete and required the work of over 100 sculptors, including Leochares' brother, Pythokles.

    The statue's impact extended beyond its physical presence; it represented a symbol of Hellenistic culture and its pursuit of beauty and perfection. As such, it influenced art and architecture for centuries to come, from Roman and Renaissance styles to modern sculpture.
